title: PathCandidates clones candidates onto path stack
description:
In pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:714, PathCandidates::next() clones each candidate certificate onto the path stack (self.path.push(candidate.clone())). Similarly, line 645 clones the entire path on each yield (return Some(Ok(self.path.clone()))).

What goes wrong: Each DFS step allocates a full Certificate clone. For deep pools with many candidates, this produces O(depth * candidates_tried) Certificate clones. The yield path additionally clones the entire chain. x509_cert::Certificate is a complex type with multiple inner Vecs; cloning it is not trivial.

The path-on-yield clone (line 645) is unavoidable given the iterator's resume contract (the iterator must hold onto the DFS state while the caller inspects the yielded chain). The per-step candidate clone (line 714) could be avoided by storing pool indices in self.path rather than owned Certificates, and only materializing the Vec<Certificate> at yield time.

Locations:
- pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:714 (per-candidate clone)
- pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:645 (per-yield clone)

Recommendation: Store &Certificate borrows or pool indices in the path stack instead of owned clones. Reconstruct the owned Vec<Certificate> only at yield time. This reduces the per-step cost from O(cert_size) to O(1) and the per-yield cost stays the same.
